note: The Fair Credit Reporting Act reaches Puerto Rico: its "State" is any State, Puerto Rico, the District of Columbia and any territory or possession of the United States (15 U.S.C. 1681a(n)). It bars an adverse item more than seven years old (1681c(a)(5)); Experian, one of the three national bureaus, says late payments are reported once at least 30 days past the due date and stay seven years.

sources.title: 15 U.S. Code § 1681a, Definitions; rules of construction
sources.said: means any State , the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico , the District of Columbia, and any territory or possession of the United States.

sources.title: 15 U.S. Code § 1681c, Requirements relating to information contained in consumer reports
sources.said: (5) Any other adverse item of information, other than records of convictions of crimes which antedates the report by more than seven years.

sources.title: Experian, Do Companies Report a Late Payment if It’s Only a Few Days Late?
sources.said: Late payments are reported to the credit bureaus once you’re at least 30 days past your bill’s due date. ... Late payments can stay on your credit report for seven years from when the account first went past due.
